source.objectiveEnglish: Ask a worker politely for help and give simple usted commands on site.
source.focusSpanish: ¿Puede…? for polite requests and usted commands like traiga, ponga, pare
source.speakingEnglish: Ask a worker politely to bring a pallet and help you with a beam, then give two simple usted commands.

archivedDraft.title: Ask to hear it again
archivedDraft.scene: Tanaka does not catch Sato's meeting instruction in a noisy storage room and asks for a slower repetition
materialDrift: Old Japanese Foundation 9 asks Sato to repeat a noisy storage-room meeting instruction. Current source is Luis and Pedro's Houston jobsite requests for a pallet, beam help, sledgehammer, tarp, trash can, first aid kit and light.

cards.sourceEnglish: Can you bring the ladder, please?
cards.japaneseDraft: すみません、はしごを持ってきていただけますか。

cards.sourceNoteInternal: Usted command to one person; to the crew: pongan.
cards.japaneseDraft: パレットをここに置いてください。

cards.sourceNoteInternal: To the whole crew: Pónganse el casco.
cards.japaneseDraft: ヘルメットをかぶってください。

cards.sourceEnglish: Can you help me with the beam?

cards.sourceSpanish: Pare el trabajo y llame al supervisor.
cards.sourceEnglish: Stop work and call the supervisor.
cards.sourceNoteInternal: Personal a before a person: llame al supervisor.

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis es el capataz de una obra en Houston.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis is the foreman of a job site in Houston.
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイスはヒューストンの建設現場の職長です。

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Pedro, ¿puede traer la tarima, por favor?
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: Pedro, can you bring the pallet, please?
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「ペドロ、パレットを持ってきていただけますか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Pedro: Con permiso, paso con la tarima.
reader.sourceEnglish: Pedro: Excuse me, I'm coming through with the pallet.
reader.japaneseDraft: ペドロ：「すみません、パレットを持って通ります。」
ルイス：「パレットをここに置いてください。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: ¿Me puede ayudar con la viga?
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: Can you help me with the beam?

reader.sourceSpanish: Pedro: Sí, amarro la viga con la cuerda.
reader.sourceEnglish: Pedro: Yes, I tie the beam with the rope.
reader.japaneseDraft: ペドロ：「はい、梁をロープで縛ります。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Ponga el marro debajo de la lona.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: Put the sledgehammer under the tarp.

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Ponga el bote de basura junto a la puerta.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: Put the trash can next to the door.
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「ごみ箱をドアのそばに置いてください。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Traiga el botiquín y prenda la luz, por favor.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: Bring the first aid kit and turn on the light, please.
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「救急箱を持ってきて、照明をつけてください。」

decisionsNeeded: Set Japanese register for Pedro and Luis. Spanish puede and usted commands are polite, while workplace role and Japanese request forms need qualified review.
Resolve tarp and light standalone senses before selecting cards 5 and 10; the Reader's turn-on-light context supports a conditional illumination proposal but not a universal card headword.
Resolve help with the beam without inventing lifting/carrying work, and resolve call the supervisor as telephone versus summon before selecting cards 15 and 16 or Reader 5.
Confirm pallet, beam, sledgehammer, hard hat, first aid kit and tarp terms with qualified Japanese/construction/dictionary reviewers; Reader 7 remains unset for tarp terminology.

Preserve Houston, Luis, Pedro, pallet, beam, rope, sledgehammer, tarp, trash can, first aid kit and light in source order; do not substitute the archived meeting scene or transfer its saved positions or audio.

Author six exact prompt/target modes, forms, speaking, dictionary and saved-item semantics only after qualified text selection; verify exact text before synthesis and make separate technical and human listening decisions per clip.
